Unit 17 – Grammar

-ing form or infinitive · prefer, would rather, had better · infinitives of purpose · 10 exercises

Exercise A – Circle the correct word or phrase
Choose the correct -ing form or infinitive for each sentence.
  • 1. I really don't feel like out tonight. Do you?
    ✓ going (feel like + -ing)
  • 2. Everyone expected his business within the first few months.
    ✓ to fail (expect + to-infinitive)
  • 3. What would you like this evening?
    ✓ to do (would like + to-infinitive)
  • 4. We discussed the attic into a spare bedroom with the architect.
    ✓ turning (discuss + -ing)
  • 5. She wasn't able very clearly after her accident.
    ✓ to speak (be able + to-infinitive)
  • 6. Do you mind your car, please? You're blocking the road.
    ✓ moving (mind + -ing)
  • 7. They're going to postpone a decision until next month.
    ✓ making (postpone + -ing)
  • 8. Are you planning a new DVD player?
    ✓ to get (plan + to-infinitive)
  • 9. Are you thinking a PlayStation?
    ✓ of getting (think of + -ing) — Note: both forms appear; the book shows "of getting / to get" and answer is "of getting"
  • 10. I'm very pleased you that you've passed!
    ✓ to tell (pleased + to-infinitive)
  • 11. Sarah's offered us up for the weekend.
    ✓ to put (offer + to-infinitive)
  • 12. I'm really looking forward on the cruise.
    ✓ to going (look forward to + -ing)
Exercise B – Complete using the correct form of the verb in brackets
Use -ing form or full infinitive. You may need to use the passive voice.
  • 1. I'll never forgive June for (lie) to me like that.
    ✓ lying (forgive for + -ing)
  • 2. Daniel's not very good at (make) friends.
    ✓ making (good at + -ing)
  • 3. I can't resist (buy) things when they're in the sales.
    ✓ buying (resist + -ing)
  • 4. We've got to encourage students (study), not blame them for not studying.
    ✓ to study (encourage sb + to-infinitive)
  • 5. I don't know how you managed (persuade) the bank manager to lend you so much money!
    ✓ to persuade (manage + to-infinitive)
  • 6. Does Jessica dislike (walk) so much that she's not going to come with us?
    ✓ walking (dislike + -ing)
  • 7. Do you deny (steal) the money? Yes or no?
    ✓ stealing (deny + -ing)
  • 8. The kids were pretending (be) asleep but they didn't fool me for a second.
    ✓ to be (pretend + to-infinitive)
  • 9. I refuse (accept) that there's no alternative.
    ✓ to accept (refuse + to-infinitive)
  • 10. No one understands how Jill can afford (go) on so many holidays each year.
    ✓ to go (afford + to-infinitive)
  • 11. He only just escaped (send) to prison. Next time, the judge won't be so forgiving.
    ✓ being sent (escape + -ing; passive -ing form)
  • 12. He expected (give) a brand new computer for Christmas, but all he got was a second-hand watch!
    ✓ to be given (expect + passive to-infinitive)

Read the text in Exercise D and write ing, BI or FI for each numbered gap.
  • 1. Gap (1):
    ✓ ing (afraid of + -ing)
  • 2. Gap (2):
    ✓ BI (can't help + -ing... actually ing here) — BI: he can't help doing = -ing; "can't help" → ing
  • 3. Gap (3):
    ✓ FI (to avoid + -ing… avoid → ing)
  • 4. Gap (4):
    ✓ ing (using his brain – avoid + -ing)
  • 5. Gap (5):
    ✓ ing (detest + -ing)
  • 6. Gap (6):
    ✓ ing (capable of + -ing)
  • 7. Gap (7):
    ✓ ing (succeed in + -ing)
  • 8. Gap (8):
    ✓ BI (wants to + bare inf: "play the fool")
  • 9. Gap (9):
    ✓ ing (enjoys + -ing)
  • 10. Gap (10):
    ✓ FI (imagines this to be)
  • 11. Gap (11):
    ✓ ing (ends up + -ing)
  • 12. Gap (12):
    ✓ FI (promised + to-infinitive)
  • 13. Gap (13):
    ✓ ing (keeps on + -ing)
  • 14. Gap (14):
    ✓ BI (beg sb + to-inf → actually FI; "beg him to sit down")
  • 15. Gap (15):
    ✓ FI (make + object + bare inf → BI: "make him come")
  • 16. Gap (16):
    ✓ ing (interested in + -ing)
  • 17. Gap (17):
    ✓ ing (tempted to give up even hoping → "even hoping")
Exercise D – Complete using verbs from the box
Use each verb only once in the correct form (-ing, bare infinitive or full infinitive).
achieve be behave come do hope improve learn listen make play sit down take tell try use work
Report: William Watson

William Watson sometimes seems to be afraid of (1) hard. He can't help (2) to avoid (3) anything that involves (4) his brain, particularly on Friday afternoons. He seems to detest (5) life seriously, and pretends he isn't capable of (6) anything of worth. This is unfortunate as, with a little more effort, William could succeed in (7) great progress. However, at present he frequently just wants (8) the fool. He enjoys (9) jokes. Presumably, he imagines this (10) the best way to make friends, but in fact he often just ends up preventing the other students from (11) . He has promised on several occasions (12) his behaviour in class, but then he just keeps on (13) in exactly the same way. Recently, I have had to beg him (14) and be quiet in the classroom, but it's difficult to know how to make him (15) to his senses. He just doesn't seem interested in (16) to my opinion. I'm tempted to give up even (17) that he might improve.

✓ (1)working (2)trying (3)doing (4)using (5)taking (6)achieving (7)making (8)to play (9)telling (10)to be (11)learning (12)to improve (13)behaving (14)to sit down (15)come (16)listening (17)hoping
Exercise E – Same or different meaning?
Put a tick (✓) if both sentences mean the same, a cross (✗) if they have different meanings.
  • 1. a) I can't bear being tickled!   b) I can't bear to be tickled!
    ✓ Same – bear can take both forms with same meaning
  • 2. a) My boss went on saying he was very proud.   b) My boss went on to say he was very proud.
    ✗ Different – "went on saying" = continued; "went on to say" = next did
  • 3. a) Have you stopped having lunch yet?   b) Have you stopped to have lunch yet?
    ✗ Different – "stopped having" = ceased; "stopped to have" = paused in order to
  • 4. a) Have you started having lunch yet?   b) Have you started to have lunch yet?
    ✓ Same – start takes both forms with same meaning
  • 5. a) They continued climbing the mountain.   b) They continued to climb the mountain.
    ✓ Same – continue takes both forms with same meaning
  • 6. a) We all saw the reporter interviewing the witness.   b) We all saw the reporter interview the witness.
    ✓ Same – see + object + -ing / bare inf (both acceptable here)
  • 7. a) I love playing practical jokes on my younger brother.   b) I love to play practical jokes.
    ✓ Same – love takes both forms with same meaning (general preference)
  • 8. a) Why don't you try holding your breath?   b) Why don't you try to hold your breath?
    ✓ Same (approximately – try + -ing = experiment; try + to-inf = attempt; subtle difference but both work here)
  • 9. a) I hate being cheated by taxi drivers.   b) I hate to be cheated by taxi drivers.
    ✓ Same – hate takes both forms with same meaning
Exercise F – Complete each second sentence using the key word
Write between two and five words in each gap. The meaning must be similar.
  • 1.
    I should have taken my medicine this morning but I didn't remember. forgot
    I my medicine this morning.
    ✓ forgot to take
  • 2.
    I'll always remember the time when I went up Mont Blanc. never
    I'll Mont Blanc.
    ✓ never forget climbing
  • 3.
    I must hang up the washing later. remember
    I up the washing later.
    ✓ must remember to hang
  • 4.
    Darren thinks that wearing a suit to work is appropriate. likes
    Darren a suit to work.
    ✓ likes wearing / likes to wear
  • 5.
    Jackie wishes she hadn't said that to Allie. regrets
    Jackie that to Allie.
    ✓ regrets saying
  • 6.
    I'm sorry but your credit card has been cancelled by the bank. regret
    I your credit card has been cancelled by the bank.
    ✓ regret to inform you that
  • 7.
    Crashing the car wasn't my intention, you know! mean
    I the car, you know!
    ✓ didn't mean to crash
  • 8.
    If I take that job, I'll have to do a lot more travelling. mean
    Taking that job to do a lot more travelling.
    ✓ will mean doing
  • 9.
    Jim's mum made him tidy his room before he could go and play. made
    Jim his room before he could go and play in the park.
    ✓ was made to tidy
  • 10.
    I don't suppose you watched that film last night on BBC2, did you? happen
    You that film last night on BBC2, did you?
    ✓ didn't happen to watch
  • 11.
    People often think that learning Latin is a waste of time. considered
    Learning Latin a waste of time.
    ✓ is often considered to be
Exercise G – Rewrite the incorrect word or phrase correctly
Each bold word or phrase is incorrect. Write the correct version.
  • 1. I generally prefer coffee from tea. →
    ✓ to (prefer X to Y)
  • 2. Do you prefer watching a DVD at home to go to the cinema? →
    ✓ going (prefer -ing to -ing)
  • 3. I had prefer to meet you a bit later. →
    ✓ would (would prefer to)
  • 4. He'd prefer not have to get up so early tomorrow. →
    ✓ would rather not have (he'd rather not have to)
  • 5. I'd rather you write your essay in a notebook. →
    ✓ wrote (I'd rather + subject + past simple)
  • 6. Would you prefer to get a pizza rather from go out tonight? →
    ✓ than (rather than)
  • 7. You would better see a doctor if you're not feeling well. →
    ✓ had (had better)
  • 8. I had rather be poor and happy than rich and lonely. →
    ✓ would (would rather)
  • 9. I'd prefer having an early night tonight. →
    ✓ to have (would prefer + to-infinitive)
  • 10. She'd rather start revising if she wants to do well in the exam. →
    ✓ had better (she'd better start = it would be wise for her to)
  • 11. Shona prefers to not wear make-up to work. →
    ✓ not to wear (negative infinitive: prefers not to wear)
Exercise H – Write one word in each gap
Prefer, would rather, had better, infinitives of purpose.
  • 1. I prefer pop music rock, to be honest.
    ✓ to (prefer X to Y)
  • 2. I would prefer to go to the concert tomorrow than on Saturday.
    ✓ rather (would rather… than)
  • 3. I playing the piano on my own to performing.
    ✓ prefer (prefer -ing to -ing)
  • 4. I'd rather to that jazz club than a nightclub.
    ✓ go (would rather + bare infinitive)
  • 5. I'd you didn't practise playing the trumpet while I'm trying to study.
    ✓ rather (I'd rather + subject + past simple)
  • 6. You'd get tickets soon as they're running out.
    ✓ better (had better)
  • 7. We queued up early in to get good seats.
    ✓ order (in order to = infinitive of purpose)
  • 8. We waited for hours so not to miss the VIPs arriving.
    ✓ as (so as not to = negative infinitive of purpose)
  • 9. I called the theatre find out what time the concert started.
    ✓ to (to-infinitive of purpose)
  • 10. I actually prefer to listen to music through speakers; it sounds so much better through headphones.
    ✓ not (prefer not to)
  • 11. Don't you think we better turn the music down a bit?
    ✓ had (had better)
Exercise I – Choose the correct answer
Read the passage "Approaches to learning" and choose the best option A, B, C or D for each gap.
  • 1. People appear (1) ………… in different ways.
    ✓ A to learn (appear + to-infinitive)
  • 2. Some people expect (2) ………… mistakes in their studies.
    ✓ A to make (expect + to-infinitive)
  • 3. …and are capable of (3) ………… from their mistakes.
    ✓ A benefiting (capable of + -ing)
  • 4. They don't mind (4) ………… by their teacher.
    ✓ B being corrected (mind + -ing; passive = being corrected)
  • 5. …and indeed often ask (5) ………… corrected.
    ✓ A to be (ask + to-infinitive; passive = to be corrected)
  • 6. Others, however, dislike (6) ………… mistakes.
    ✓ A making (dislike + -ing)
  • 7. They try to avoid (7) ………… anything which they might do badly.
    ✓ A doing (avoid + -ing)
  • 8. They would rather (8) ………… something in small steps.
    ✓ B perfect (would rather + bare infinitive)
  • 9. …before they (9) ………… attempt to do a task.
    ✓ D than (would rather… than)
  • 10. …on a subject they don't feel they have finished (10) ………… yet.
    ✓ C exploring (finish + -ing)
  • 11. Both ways of learning seem (11) ………… equally valid.
    ✓ B to be (seem + to-infinitive)
  • 12. In (12) ………… to learn effectively, students have to remember…
    ✓ C order (in order to = infinitive of purpose)
  • 13. …students have to remember (13) ………… risks sometimes.
    ✓ A to take (remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do)
  • 14. …so (14) ………… not to become demotivated.
    ✓ A as (so as not to = negative purpose)
  • 15. All students should at least think about (15) ………… the way that they approach learning.
    ✓ A questioning (think about + -ing)
